Hi Alex / Priya — great call today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment going into the SE deep-dive: 

Summary of what we heard
- You want server-to-server inference from your ingestion pipeline into both the reranker/embedding endpoints and the generate/chat endpoints.
- Primary concerns: key management (rotation, least privilege), auditability (who calls what), and minimizing blast radius for leaked creds.
- Secondary: SDK ease-of-use for engineers (Node/Python), and per-route routing (e.g., lower-cost model for embeddings vs. higher-quality chat model).

Redwood recommended approach (high-level)
- Use service accounts for machine-to-machine calls. Issue short-lived JWTs/tokens from a central token service. This avoids long-lived static API keys in code.
- For user-facing auth flows (where calls are made on behalf of end users), use OAuth/JWT with scopes.
- If you must use API keys initially for quick testing, treat them as admin-managed secrets with rotation and IP/network restrictions; do not embed in client-side code.
- Integrations (embeddings/rerankers): create scoped keys/accounts per use-case (separate key for embeddings ingestion pipeline vs. live chat) to limit blast radius.

Attachments included:
- redwood-integration-checklist.pdf (high-level tasks and owners)
- service-account-sample.json (example service account payload used for token exchange)
- redwood-admin-api-keys-postman-collection.json (admin API examples for key lifecycle)

Next steps / asks

2) Alex / Priya: confirm whether you can run a short SE session next Tue (Mar 17) 10–11am PT or 2–3pm PT.
3) We’ll surface SOC2 evidence and our admin API docs in the shared drive.

Hi Alex — cc Marissa. Quick answers + concrete patterns below. Happy to walk through these on Tue.

1) Programmatic key lifecycle
- Yes: Redwood exposes an Admin API for key management (create, list, revoke, rotate). Example (admin token required):
  - Create new API key: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/admin/v1/keys -H "Authorization: Bearer <ADMIN_TOKEN>" -d '{"name":"fintechco-embeddings-2026-03"}'
  - Revoke older key: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/admin/v1/keys/<key_id>/revoke
- We also provide a Postman collection (attached) and client libraries for the admin API.

2) Zero-downtime rotation pattern for pipelines
- Create new key/service-account credentials.
- Update pipeline to accept both old and new credentials (dual-write/dual-read short window) while you test.
- Flip ingestion to new credentials; monitor error rates and latency.
- Revoke the old key after TTL/monitoring window.
- Alternatively, use short-lived tokens issued by your internal token service: have your token service mint tokens from a long-lived service account and rotate the underlying service-account keys behind the token service — pipeline only sees short-lived tokens and never touches long-lived secret.

3) Service-account scoping recommendations
- For separation of concerns and auditable traces, we recommend separate service accounts per major pipeline (e.g., embeddings-insert, embeddings-query, reranker, chat-ingest).
- Use IAM scopes/route-level ACLs so each account only has access to the endpoints it needs. This minimizes blast radius and makes for clearer logs.

4) Embeddings/reranker specifics
- Auth model: same auth infra (service accounts / short-lived tokens) works fine for embeddings. If you need stricter isolation, create separate accounts.
- For high-throughput ingestion: recommend batching + connection pooling and attach a key rotation window to your deployment pipeline to rotate with minimal disruption.

5) Audit & compliance
- We place calls in structured logs with key id and actor id; logs are retained per your contract. SOC2 docs and audit screenshots are in the Drive link Marissa shared. Happy to surface any additional artifacts procurement needs.

6) SDK snippets
- Node sample (token exchange -> call):
  const axios = require('axios');
  async function getToken() {
    const resp = await axios.post('https://token.internal.fintechco.com/v1/exchange', {service_account: 'sa-embeddings-01'});
    return resp.data.access_token;
  }
  async function callEmbedding() {
    const token = await getToken();
    const r = await axios.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings', {input: ['doc text']}, { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } });
    console.log(r.data);
  }

- Python sample (token lifetime enforcement):
  import requests
  def get_token():
    r = requests.post('https://token.internal.fintechco.com/v1/exchange', json={'service_account': 'sa-embeddings-01'})
    return r.json()['access_token']

  token = get_token()
  headers = {'Authorization': f'Bearer {token}'}
  r = requests.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings', json={'input':['text']}, headers=headers)

7) Recommended rotation cadence
- Short-lived tokens: minutes -> rotate automatically.
- Service-account keys (if used as long-lived): rotate every 90 days, rotate sooner if exposed. Automate via CI/CD.

I’ve attached the example service-account payload and the admin API Postman collection to this thread. If you want, I can also provision a sandbox service account scoped to your test project ahead of Tue so you can validate the flow.
